features.requirement: Make the game screen board-first: maximize playable board area on portrait Android, remove distracting chrome, maintain legible player and status information, and avoid touch obstruction or overflow at ~320 px width.

Retain all 12 existing Animal Kingdom PNGs unchanged and accessible. Add an alternative high-clarity Classic/Staunton piece set, visually distinct for each piece and side even at small sizes. Never replace or silently alter approved Animal Kingdom assets.

Open directly to a no-login play menu with obvious Play Computer, Play Friend and Continue Game actions. Optional Account panel retains registration, login, recovery and private history without blocking guest play.

Guarantee all NEW ordinary games and rematches are genuinely UNTIMED at the authoritative backend/game-state level. Preserve all existing stored 10+0 clocks and their server timeout behavior. Never implement the superseded 15+0 request; never merely hide clock UI. Detect legacy/incompatible production capabilities, explain limitations clearly, and prevent misleading claims. Untimed PGN TimeControl is “-”; historical timed PGN remains “600+0”.
Make shareable private friend invitations, ideally links plus room codes. Validate permissions, app-link handling and recipient flows, with a manual fallback if links cannot open the app.

Auto-save games and moves reliably across app kills, screen lock, network interruptions and device restarts. Distinguish local/computer state from server-authoritative multiplayer state; never overwrite a newer remote game with stale local data.

Add adjustable and meaningful engine difficulty presets (beginner, casual, club, strong, plus a suitable fine-grained control). Verify actual behavior at each difficulty rather than only changing labels.
Highlight selected squares, legal destinations, captures, last move and a checked king using clear, accessible contrast and restrained visuals.

Build a navigable post-game analysis mode with Stockfish-based evaluation, alternative moves, readable mistake categories and a way back to the original game. Keep analysis separate from actual multiplayer moves.

Deliver and verify a genuinely OFFLINE computer chess engine on-device, identifying its actual technology/version and license. The existing bundled fallback is NOT proof of offline native Stockfish 18. If native Stockfish 18 is infeasible within constraints, use a real locally bundled, licensed engine and truthfully label its version; do not claim unavailable strength or functionality.

Make reconnection resilient: reconnecting guest/account players recover authorized seats and authoritative board state; viewers never gain move rights; surface meaningful connection states and avoid double-submitted moves.

Qualify the APK for Poco X7 Pro / Android 16 where real-device access exists: installation, touch, portrait layout, screen lock/background/restore, audio, offline play and two-client multiplayer. If hardware is unavailable, use emulators/browser tests and explicitly list physical checks as unverified.
Support both tap-to-move and drag-to-move; configurable, touch friendly and usable without precision gestures.
Show clear legal-move previews and optional attack/capture distinctions, without revealing analysis when assistance is disabled.
Use subtle, optional capture/move animations; prioritize responsiveness, clarity and reduced-motion settings.
Implement a large, accessible four-piece promotion chooser with correct underpromotion behavior.
Display captured material and material balance without crowding the board.
Provide expandable algebraic move history, review navigation and current move highlighting; browsing history must not accidentally mutate the live game.
Support manual board flip, sensible automatic orientation for Black and correct coordinate labels.
Offer an optional confirmation-before-move setting; default off, especially for quick casual play.

Support undo/redo/takeback against the computer; multiplayer takebacks require explicit bilateral consent and server-checked authorization if offered. Never allow spectators or unauthorized clients to roll back moves.
Handle stalemate, checkmate, legal draws, offers/acceptance, repetition, insufficient material and applicable 50-/75-move conditions correctly; preserve PGN result and rules consistency.
Add fully local pass-and-play for two people on one phone, with turn-based board flipping, no login and no network requirement.

Add separately selectable Chess960/Fischer Random, with verified starting setup, legal Chess960 castling, FEN/PGN representation, replay and correct engine/backend support. Default remains standard untimed chess; gate unsupported online variants rather than fake support.
Provide a readable post-game evaluation graph and jump-to-position navigation; mark whether evaluation is engine-generated or provisional.
Detect major blunders, mistakes and missed tactical opportunities using declared scoring thresholds/search limits, and avoid pseudoscientific precision or “best move” guarantees.

Add useful, understandable explanations of candidate best moves using deterministic chess features/variations (threats, material, king safety, tactics); no paid API or external generative AI. Distinguish explanation heuristics from engine evaluation.

Give offline AI opponents recognizable playing styles (e.g., Fox = tactical, Tortoise = defensive, Owl = positional, plus beginner), implemented through real, tested difficulty/selection parameters, not merely names or random illegal moves.
Optionally adapt computer difficulty based on local games with user consent/toggle and transparency; do not secretly modify rated or human games.

Add offline tactics exercises with solutions, hints, explanations, replay and a small properly licensed starter set; support forks, pins, skewers, discovered attacks, mate patterns and progressively harder puzzles.
Add a compact offline opening explorer with transparent source/license, name, move frequency or curated continuation data, and no fabricated statistics.
Add an offline endgame trainer (basic mates, king/pawn and elementary rook endings) with correct position setup, success criteria and hints.
Add a position editor and robust FEN import/export, turn/castling/en-passant validation and ability to start local engine analysis or a game from a legal position.
Permit analysis of locally saved positions without overwriting an ongoing match; “Continue the Position” should be one tap from the home screen where a saved session exists.
Add engine strength, thinking time, CPU/battery and responsiveness controls; cancel or suspend obsolete searches on navigation/backgrounding and profile performance on Android.

Generate shareable QR invitations without forcing a camera permission; provide link/code input and operating-system/external QR scanning alternatives. Only add in-app camera scanning after separate permission approval.
Allow local guest display nicknames without creating accounts. Sanitize display names, keep private seat credentials out of names, links, logs and screenshots.
Add a clear game lobby showing side selection, invitation state, untimed/variant rules and spectator count, without disclosing protected information.
Display actionable connectivity indicators: connected, reconnecting, peer disconnected, server unavailable and incompatible backend. Do not claim delivery of a move before server confirmation.
Make one-tap rematches with same/swapped colors; enforce guest/account ownership and untimed rematch creation. Support refusal/cancellation cleanly.

Add optional correspondence-style asynchronous play, with server-persisted turns and reopen/resume flows. Preserve the “new games untimed” rule: NO countdowns, per-move forfeits or implicit time controls. Optional reminders must not become compulsory, spammy or paid; do not enable live notifications without necessary permission and release approval.
Add safe spectator mode: read-only board and legal public game status, no move, resign, pause, rematch, nudge or private token access.
Add a small opt-in, nonverbal, abuse-resistant reaction palette, including optional Animal Kingdom reactions. No free-form chat, uploads or unmoderated message service.

Design abandoned-room expiration/cleanup with explicit documentation and tests. Never delete active or historical games or accounts; live cleanup jobs/database writes require separate production approval.
Show server capabilities and live/unsupported game features clearly; avoid misleading “untimed multiplayer available” claims while the production server still uses the old behavior.
Optimize immersive portrait Android UI with correct insets, keyboard behavior, navigation gestures, orientation safety and large tap targets; do not require a landscape layout.
Add a configurable left-handed control layout and ergonomic one-handed access without changing chess orientation unexpectedly.
Offer board/UI themes: Classic Wood, Midnight, Ivory, Forest and Animal Kingdom. Persist preferences locally; themes must not obscure the pieces or change rules.

Add accessibility: high contrast, non-color-only indicators, TalkBack/semantic labels where possible, scalable controls, reduced motion, readable text and tap alternatives to dragging. Validate against relevant WCAG 2.2 touch principles.
Add quiet, optional move/capture sounds and configurable haptics that respect mute/accessibility/system behavior. No surprise audio or permanent background playback.
Reduce polling, unnecessary WebView CPU/battery usage and stale engine work; test foreground/background recovery, thermal/battery impact and cancellation of computation.

Add a privacy-safe About / Diagnostics screen showing package/version/code, source commit, engine implementation/version, offline status, server compatibility and sanitized connection status. Do not expose tokens, private player records, credential-bearing URLs or secrets.
Add portable PGN game export/import and FEN sharing with strong input validation, clear save/restore boundaries, no compulsory registration and no accidental local-data overwrite.

Harden anonymous capability tokens, account-seat identity checks, WebSocket reauthorization, rate limiting, replay/idempotency, logging redaction, spectator boundaries, secure Android WebViewAssetLoader and restrictive file-access settings. Test attacks with synthetic users; do not loosen security to make guest access easier.

Create repeatable release artifacts with versioning, proven signing/package identity, checksum, commit hash, reproducible build instructions, relevant licenses, test reports, screenshots, rollback/migration guidance and upgrade compatibility notes. Preserve separately gated schema-v4 release process and do not claim an older differently signed APK can update in place.
